To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Super-Kamiikande atmospheric neutrino results can be explained by a three-neutrinos mixing scheme with one mass squared difference.

(a) the Super-Kamioka-neutrino-Experiment (SK) atmospheric neutrino data are consistent with the standard three-neutrino mixing model, (b) the data allow a non-zero ν e → ν e mixing angle of up to 0.18, (c) this mixing is consistent with the CHOOZ limit, and (d) the data allow ν e → ν μ oscillations at a level of up to 10 -4.
The Super-Kamioknde atmospheric neutrino data are consistent with ν μ ↔ ν τ oscillations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neutrino oscillation phenomena and the search for the neutrino mass.
the study of the neutrino mixing angle and the neutrino mass spectrum in a three-neutrinomodel.
the problem of the origin of the atmospheric neutrino anomaly.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are consistent with ν μ → ν tau oscillations with Δ m 2 = 2.5 × 10 -3 eV 2.
the Super-Kamioka-neutrino-observation data are compatible with a large number of different three-neutrino mixing scenarios.
the data are consistent with the ν μ → ν _{τ} oscillations, but the data are not inconsistent with the ν μ ↔ ν _{e} oscillations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the atmospheric anomaly is not necessarily a ν μ → ν _{τ} phenomenon.

the atmospheric anomaly is consistent with ν μ → ν s (s = e or τ ) oscillations, and that the atmospheric anomaly can be explained by the ν μ ↔ ν s mixing with the mass-squared difference ∼ 10 −4 eV 2.
the Super-Kamiokiande atmospheric neutrino anomaly can be explained by the oscillation of the ν μ to ν e or the ν μ to the sterile ν s with the mixing angle sin 2 2θ > 0.01.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the atmospheric anomaly can be accommodated in a model with three-neutrino mixing, but it requires that the mixing between the two mass eigenstates that contribute significantly to the oscillation be large, i.e., sin 2 2 θ > 0.5.
the atmospheric anomaly is not yet sufficient to exclude ν μ → ν s oscillations, where ν s is an active neutrino flavor.
the atmospheric anomaly is not yet a smoking gun for ν μ ↔ ν τ oscillations.
